NPCI - FTE EXPERIENCE
OMKAR KAMBLE
B.TECH Computer Engineering (2020-2024)
NPCI visited our campus in Sept 2023 to hire final year students for the role of Full
Stack Developer, Development Resource & Testing Resource
Eligibility Criteria
1. CPI : 6.75 and for Diploma 60%
2. Branches : CS, IT, Electronics, Electrical & EXTC
Rounds
1. Online Assessment (6th Sept)
2. Technical + HR (Online - 12th Sept)
For more info about NPCI : NPCI.org

Round 1 - Online Assessment
The test was conducted on the AON platform. A total of 100 students were shortlisted for this
test, which consisted of four sections. You can navigate between the questions.
Section 1 : Aptitude (30 Questions in 30 mins)
The first 10 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) were based on English Usage covering topics
such as antonyms, synonyms and passage-based questions. The next 10 MCQs were focused on
Analytical Reasoning including questions related to flowcharts, patterns and statements with
conclusions. The final 10 MCQs pertained to Quantitative Aptitude covering topics like
profit-loss, missing terms and probability.
Section 2 : Machine Learning (20 questions in 20 mins)
All 20 MCQs were based on machine learning (ML) algorithms like Random Forest, Hypothesis
Testing, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Neural Networks etc.
Section 3 : Written English Test (25 mins)
In this section we were asked to write reviews on the given topic (Around 250 words)
Topic : We should use less plastic in our life.
Section 4 : Coding Questions (2 Questions in 60 mins)
1. Longest Substring of Even length
Statement : You are given a string s of length n. The string s consists of digits varying from 0-9.
Find and print the length of the longest even length substring of string s, such that the length of
substring is 2k digits and the sum of left k digits is equal to the sum of right k digits.
Note : Print 0 if no such substring is possible with the given condition
Input Format :
●
The first line contains an integer denoting n
●
The second line contains a string denoting s
Output : The length of the longest even length substring

Link : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/longest-even-length-substring-sum-first-second-half/
I was able to solve this completely.
2. Minimum strength to reach destination
Statement : You are given a matrix mat of size m*n. Each cell of a matrix contains strength. A
robot needs a positive strength to travel from the top left corner of the matrix to the bottom right
corner. At any point of the journey, its strength cannot drop to 0 or less. The cells can contain
either 0, positive or negative strength. Positive strength increases the robots strength by cell
value, negative strength decreases its strength by cell value and no change in strength if the cell
value is 0. You are required to calculate the minimum initial strength required by the robot to
travel from the source to reach the destination.
Note :
●
A robot can only move one cell at a time, either down or right, i.e to cell (i+1,j) or
cell (i,j+1) and it cannot move outside the matrix.
●
mat[0][0] = mat[m-1][n-1] = 0
Input Format :
●
The first line contains two space-separated integers i.e no of rows m and columns n
●
The second line contains m*n integers separated by space (Elements of matrix)
Output Format :
Print the minimum initial strength required by the robot to travel from source to destination.
The question was similar to this one :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/minimum-positive-points-to-reach-destination/
I was successfully able to pass all the test cases for this problem.
12 students were shortlisted for online interviews which were scheduled on MS teams.

Round 2 - Technical + HR
Since it was an online interview, there was one panel with 3-4 interviewers, including HR.
Initially, HR introduced herself, but before we could start the interview, there was a delay on my
side. HR then asked me to re-login to the meeting, which took me around 5-8 minutes to join due
to my poor network connection. I felt a bit frustrated during this time because of the technical
issues.
After re-joining the meeting, HR started with a very common question, which you all are
familiar with : 'Please introduce yourself.' Typically, in many interviews, technical questions are
asked first, followed by HR-related questions. However, in my case, the interview began with
HR questions right away.
After hearing my introduction, she asked, 'Where are you from?' I replied, 'I'm from Mumbai,
Thane.' She then mentioned that most of their branches are located in Chennai, Hyderabad and
Bangalore, but since I'm from Mumbai, asked if I would be able to relocate. I assured her that I
am flexible with regard to locations. Next, she requested to see my Aadhar card, mostly for
verification purposes. Following that, she inquired about my knowledge of NPCI products. I
explained this question very thoroughly and she seemed quite impressed with my response. She
then proceeded to ask some of the common HR questions: 'Why should we hire you and why
NPCI?' After this, she stated that this concludes her portion of the interview and another
interviewer will continue from here. However, she remained present in the meeting throughout
the entire interview.
The next interviewer was very friendly and conducted my technical interview. He started by
asking me to explain my projects. Initially, I provided an overview of all the projects. Afterward
I asked, Shall I explain each of them one by one or would you like information about a specific
one? He then responded, Explain the project you liked the most. I chose a project based on
Machine Learning. Since I was well-prepared with that. After I finished explaining, he shifted
the focus to questions about data pre-processing. I managed to answer scenario-based questions
quite well, except for one that it involved extracting a movie name, for instance, 'ABC___,' and
determining how to obtain 'A_B_C' from the dataset. This proved to be particularly challenging
compared to the others. Initially, I proposed a solution, but it turned out to be incorrect. The
interviewer kindly rephrase the question and after taking some time to think, I provided another
solution. But it seemed he was still unsatisfied with my answer.
He moved on to SQL. The first question was a general one, asking me to explain something
about SQL. Then, he presented a specific query: the date-time format was 'YYYY-MM-DD,' but
he wanted it in reverse order. He asked how I would achieve this. Following that, he asked
several questions about joins. Another question he posed was about filtering records, to which I

responded that it can be easily done with the help of a WHERE clause. Although there were a
few more questions, I only remember these. The questions asked were not entirely
straightforward; they required identification with the correct solution.
Now it was time for the third interviewer. He began by asking me questions related to Python. I
provided explanations for them. However, before proceeding further into Python-related
questions, I made it clear to him that I am proficient in C++ and have limited experience in
Python, aside from one ML-based project.
I'd like to emphasize a point here: if you encounter a situation in an interview where you're asked
about a specific tech stack or subject that you haven't mentioned in your resume and have no
knowledge about, it's better to inform the interviewer. You can say something like, 'I have no
experience with this particular area, but I'm open to learning it in the future.' This approach is
more advisable than providing incorrect answers.
And in this way, the interview almost came to an end. At last HR asked if I had any questions.
Tip : It is a good practice to ask questions, it shows that you are interested in the company and
gives a positive impression to the interviewer.
My interview lasted for about 20-25 mins.
The results were announced on the same day at 6 pm. A total of 9 students were selected and
fortunately, I was one of them 🤩
Resources :
1. DSA Problems =>
Striver SDE Sheet
https://takeuforward.org/interviews/strivers-sde-sheet-top-coding-interview-problems/
450 Sheet by Love Babbar => https://450dsa.com/
I would suggest practice Leetcode Daily and Leetcode Medium Level Problems based on
Tags.
2. OS and DBMS =>

You can try Gate smashers for OS and Knowledge gate for DBMS (Try to make your
own notes from the playlist)
I studied all the questions on OS and DBMS from InterviewBit.
3. OOPS =>
Love Babbar (YT : OOPS Part 1 & OOPS Part 2)
I made my own notes from Coding Ninjas.
4. SQL =>
To Study all concepts related to SQL : https://www.w3schools.com/sql/
For practice : Leetcode SQL questions
Tips :
1. Be thorough with all sorting algorithms and their implementations because these
questions are often asked in interviews.
2. Be well-prepared with the projects you have mentioned in your resume and anticipate all
possible questions that could be asked in the interview.
I would suggest having key points ready for all your projects that you want to describe.
Your explanations should cover important points. You can try using the STAR method to explain
your projects.
3. Before the interview, check whether all your projects are working properly because in
online interviews, the interviewer may ask to show a demo of your projects.
4. For Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), try to explain concepts with real-life
examples. Interviewers may also ask you to implement some concepts in code.
5. If you don’t get selected for an internship that comes through on-campus recruitment,
don’t get disappointed. It's a part of life. However, make sure that for placements, you
won’t repeat the mistakes that caused you to be rejected in an internship. Always try to
learn from your failures.
6. Your communication skills matter a lot in an interview. If your communication skills are
good, then there's no issue. If not, focus on improving them first.
7. For the questions that will be asked in interviews, your answers should be clear and
correct. Don’t include unnecessary details. Think out loud because the interviewer also

wants to understand your thought process. Even if you give a wrong answer, it’s okay. In
the end, your approach and way of thinking will matter.
8. Stay composed and remember that things will align as you go along. Approach the
problem with a relaxed mindset.
9. Don’t forget to research about the company. The interviewer will probably ask you about
the company’s mission, vision, etc.
10. For HR questions, you can refer to InterviewBit =>
https://www.interviewbit.com/hr-interview-questions/
11. Lastly, I would like to say, DO NOT EVER LIE ON YOUR RESUME.
Never get discouraged by your failures. Keep working HARD. Believe in yourself and
have faith in God.
HARDWORK KIAA HAI TO TUMARA DIN JAROOR AAYEGA !!
